annotations.text:
Reading depth is the bridge.

Plain / Study / Scholar changes only what opens by DEFAULT — never what is available. A layman who gets curious expands the same scholarly views a student reads. One content set, two audiences.

Try the toggle.

Peek before you leap.

Click 20:110 in the plain-English paragraph. A link never navigates on first touch — you get the verse, its translation, and WHY it is linked. Most link-following should end here, without ever leaving the page.

Ikhtilāf is reported, not resolved.

Three readings of Kursī, each with who held it, the evidence, and a locator. Weight of support is shown by the left rule and the badge — majority, reported, minority — never by hiding the minority.

Every link names a scholar.

Links come from what a mufassir actually cites while commenting — not from similarity search. That is why the peek card's footer can always say who drew the connection, and why a link is reviewable like any other claim.

What 'clean' rules out.

No permanent sidebar. No tab bar of eight tafsīr works. No verse cards in a feed. No streaks or badges. Structure carried by type and space, not boxes — except the one boundary that is non-negotiable: our summary never looks like a scholar's words.
